# Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves

Day 2, 12:05 · Tobias Schwarz, Martyna Ağanoğlu, David Carrasco Pamies · lightning · coverage: transcript, one-slide

Three community talks: broken canonical graphs (Tobias Schwarz, CTO and Founder, Audisto); consolidating two competing loan-comparison sites into one brand (Martyna Ağanoğlu, SEO Specialist, Loando / Clar); the decisions behind a multi-site migration after an acquisition (David Carrasco Pamies, SEO Consultant, Magnify). Speakers from on-stage introductions and the official speaker list; talks 2 and 3 are only in the second attendee recording.

## Claims

- **[Stage]** Broken canonical tags can make the wrong pages of a site show up in search results.
  <br><sub>`D2-C401` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · confirmed by Google docs · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting) · Extends [D1-C113](../day1/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-06`</sub>

- **[Stage]** According to the canonical link specification cited by a community speaker, when a canonical tag is declared improperly, the application that processes it may apply its own heuristic and decide what to do instead.
  <br><sub>`D2-C402` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · consistent with Google docs · [Specify your canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2009/02/specify-your-canonical), [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Repeats [D2-C380](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C873](../day2/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guide to specifying canonical URLs says Google supports explicit rel=canonical link annotations as described in RFC 6596, the canonical link relation specification.
  <br><sub>`D2-C403` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · is the documentation · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** A broken canonical setup does not fail visibly: pages still load normally while the choice of URL passes to the search engine's own heuristics, so canonical tags need a regular audit with a crawler and the URL Inspection tool.
  <br><sub>`D2-C404` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · [5 common mistakes with rel=canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2013/04/5-common-mistakes-with-relcanonical), [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting) · Used by `DEV-MON-06`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Checking canonicals pairwise (page A has a canonical to page B, page B a self-referencing canonical) is common but, in a community speaker's experience, misses the bigger picture, such as other links pointing to A or B.
  <br><sub>`D2-C406` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz)</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a community speaker's terms, a canonical group is the set of all URLs connected through canonical links, and its canonical leader is the page that all the group's canonical links ultimately point to.
  <br><sub>`D2-C407` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised auditing canonicals as whole canonical groups rather than pair by pair, paying special attention to each group's canonical leader.
  <br><sub>`D2-C408` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · Extends [D1-C128](../day1/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extends [D2-C398](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-06`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker said it helps to view small canonical groups as a graph that shows any redirects between members, together with the indexability of each member page.

- **[Slide]** The crawler report shown on screen flagged a URL discovered only through a canonical tag, with no internal a href links leading to it, as a phantom document outside the visible site structure.

- **[Analysis]** To audit canonicals at scale, resolve every crawled URL to the final URL its canonical links and redirects lead to, group URLs by that leader, and flag groups with more than one hop, a loop, several canonicals on one page, or a leader that is noindexed, blocked, non-200 or redirecting.
  <br><sub>`D2-C416` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · Used by `DEV-CAN-04`, `DEV-MON-06`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Multiple canonical declarations on one page conflict and are invalid, so the search engine applies its own heuristic and picks the canonical for the site owner; a page should declare only one canonical.
  <br><sub>`D2-C417` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · consistent with Google docs · [5 common mistakes with rel=canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2013/04/5-common-mistakes-with-relcanonical), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-03`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's 2013 Search Central blog post on rel=canonical mistakes says to specify no more than one rel=canonical per page: when a page has more than one, Google will likely ignore all of them, and any benefit of a legitimate canonical is lost.
  <br><sub>`D2-C418` · Search Central blog (8 April 2013) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · is the documentation · [5 common mistakes with rel=canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2013/04/5-common-mistakes-with-relcanonical) · Used by `DEV-CAN-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Canonical chains, where a page's canonical target leads on to yet another URL, are named as improper use in the canonical link specification, according to a community speaker.
  <br><sub>`D2-C419` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · consistent with Google docs · [Specify your canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2009/02/specify-your-canonical), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-04`, the glossary term *Canonical chain and canonical loop*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's 2009 Search Central blog post introducing rel=canonical says Google's algorithm is lenient and can follow canonical chains, but strongly recommends updating links to point to a single canonical page for optimal canonicalization.
  <br><sub>`D2-C420` · Search Central blog (12 February 2009) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · is the documentation · [Specify your canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2009/02/specify-your-canonical) · Used by `DEV-CAN-04`, the glossary term *Canonical chain and canonical loop*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Canonical chains can run through canonical links alone, through a server-side redirect between members, or through a client-side redirect between members.
  <br><sub>`D2-C421` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Slide]** The crawler report shown on screen flagged a canonical chain as a problem: canonical links that form a chain instead of all pointing directly to the group's canonical leader.

- **[Analysis]** After a migration or a subdomain change, update rel=canonical tags to the new final URLs: canonicals still pointing at old, redirecting URLs create chains through server-side redirects like the one in the real-world example shown.
  <br><sub>`D2-C423` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes) · Used by `DEV-CAN-04`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Canonical loops, such as two HTML pages whose canonical tags point to each other, are a structural conflict: the group has no canonical leader, so its canonical information cannot be used.
  <br><sub>`D2-C424` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-CAN-04`, the glossary term *Canonical chain and canonical loop*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Canonical loops can also run through server-side or client-side redirects, not only through canonical tags.
  <br><sub>`D2-C425` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker said that at best a search engine's heuristic would treat a canonical loop through redirects as self-referencing canonicals, and doubted that this is often done when the loop runs through a client-side redirect.
  > "But regarding the client-side redirect, I highly doubt that this is often done."
  <br><sub>`D2-C426` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** When internal links point only to page A and the canonical leader is reached only through A's canonical link, the leader is reachable by machines but not by human visitors, a signal conflict that asks the search engine to index a page users cannot reach.
  > "you're telling the search engine to index something that a human can't reach"
  <br><sub>`D2-C427` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · consistent with Google docs · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Extends [D1-C067](../day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Used by `DEV-CAN-04`</sub>

- **[Stage]** For a canonical leader that users cannot reach through links, a community speaker suggested revisiting the canonical graph and probably making the internally linked page the leader instead.
  <br><sub>`D2-C428` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · consistent with Google docs · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls), [5 common mistakes with rel=canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2013/04/5-common-mistakes-with-relcanonical)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker said pages carry different link equity, and a canonical leader that is not the strongest page in its group is technically valid but most likely suboptimal for ranking, so the strongest page should be the leader.
  <br><sub>`D2-C429` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · not in Google docs · Contradicts [D2-C348](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guide to specifying canonical URLs says a canonical helps consolidate signals for duplicate pages: links to a duplicate URL are consolidated with links to the preferred URL once the preferred URL becomes canonical.
  <br><sub>`D2-C430` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · is the documentation · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-05`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** A leader reachable only through a canonical and a leader with weak link equity share one fix: point internal links, sitemap entries and redirects at the URL chosen as canonical, so the leader is both reachable for users and the strongest page in its group.
  <br><sub>`D2-C431` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-05`</sub>

- **[Stage]** The canonical leader of a group should be indexable: it should carry no noindex robots directive, return no error status code and not be blocked in robots.txt.
  <br><sub>`D2-C432` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · consistent with Google docs · [5 common mistakes with rel=canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2013/04/5-common-mistakes-with-relcanonical), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The crawler report shown at the talk rated a redirecting canonical target as an error, while Google's 2009 guidance accepts a canonical URL that redirects and says Google can follow canonical chains; the gap is one of severity, since both recommend pointing every canonical link straight at the final URL.

  <br><sub>`D2-C893` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker named four kinds of post-acquisition site migration: absorb (one site integrates into the other), keep apart, merge (two or three sites into a new one), and plug in (a full site becomes a section of the other site).
  <br><sub>`D2-C894` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker said a migration should be run around one document, the redirect map, which gives every old URL an approved destination.
  <br><sub>`D2-C895` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies) · consistent with Google docs · [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes) · Used by `DEV-CAN-10`, the glossary term *Redirect map*</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker's four tips before mapping a migration: agree what to keep and retire with an owner for every decision, review what to retire with data, prioritise by business value and not only traffic, and set expectations with an owner to escalate to.
  <br><sub>`D2-C896` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised asking support and sales which pages make buyers buy, and preparing the destination with relevant content and internal links before a migration launches.
  <br><sub>`D2-C897` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies) · consistent with Google docs · [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker said most migration failures look technical but trace back to a decision nobody made; in the migration presented, more than 7,000 URLs still had no approved destination at the time of the talk.
  <br><sub>`D2-C898` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker recorded each migration decision per URL: old URL, new URL, what must survive (for example a product answer and a demo request), who approves, and the test that proves it works.
  <br><sub>`D2-C899` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies) · Used by the glossary term *Redirect map*</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised asking other teams during a migration about everything a crawler cannot reveal, such as sales workflows or legal requirements.
  <br><sub>`D2-C900` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** For migrations with many URLs, a community speaker suggested letting a similarity score propose redirect destinations and having people review the critical pages.
  <br><sub>`D2-C901` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Before a migration launches, a community speaker advised freezing the inventory (CMS export, crawl, sitemap, search data and logs), saving all content and approving the redirect map.
  <br><sub>`D2-C902` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies) · consistent with Google docs · [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes) · Used by `DEV-CAN-10`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker warned that HTTP 200 responses across a new domain show only that the URLs work, not that the content users came for is still there, so after launch the redirect map becomes the test.
  <br><sub>`D2-C903` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies) · consistent with Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Extends [D2-C334](../day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) · Used by `DEV-CAN-10`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker's three post-migration checks per URL: the route (the old URL reaches its destination), the answer (the approved content is still there) and the lead (a demo request still reaches the CRM); automate them, but have people check critical journeys.
  <br><sub>`D2-C904` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised giving moved content its own baseline, because site-wide totals can hide lost pages and lost search queries.
  <br><sub>`D2-C905` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker cited a recent study (not named) that reported a median recovery time of 304 days after a site migration.
  <br><sub>`D2-C906` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker said a long expected recovery after a migration is no reason to wait: broken redirect routes and blocked pages need action immediately.
  <br><sub>`D2-C907` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised telling users of a migrated brand that they are in the right place, through emails, a press release and a blog post, to keep the trust built with the old brand.
  <br><sub>`D2-C908` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker said reputation travels with a migrated product: a good product takes its reviews and links along, and a product nobody likes takes its complaints along.
  <br><sub>`D2-C909` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker summed up migration planning in three questions: what survives, who approves, and what test shows the migration actually works.
  <br><sub>`D2-C910` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (David Carrasco Pamies)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's site move guide says not to redirect many old URLs to one irrelevant destination such as the new site's home page, which can confuse users and might be treated as a soft 404, and to return a 404 or 410 for deleted or merged content that is not moved to the new site.
  <br><sub>`D2-C911` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · is the documentation · [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes) · Used by `DEV-CAN-10`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's site move guide says to submit a Change of Address in Search Console when moving from one domain or subdomain to another, to submit the new sitemap, and to change internal links on the new site from the old URLs to the new ones.
  <br><sub>`D2-C912` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · is the documentation · [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes) · Used by `DEV-CAN-09`, the glossary term *Change of Address tool*</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For URLs removed in a consolidation, return 404 or 410: Google's site move guide names those two codes, and Google's crawlers treat every 4xx code except 429 the same way, as content that does not exist, so the choice between them matters less than not redirecting to an unrelated page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C913` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes), [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's crawl budget guide is written for sites with over a million pages changing weekly or over 10,000 pages changing daily, so for a consolidation of about 2,000 URLs the crawl-budget gain is likely minor; the benefit of pruning such a site more plausibly comes from one strong URL per intent and consolidated signals.
  <br><sub>`D2-C914` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · [Optimize your crawl budget](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawl-budget)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The 304-day median recovery a community speaker cited from an unnamed study and Google's site move guide (a few weeks or more for a medium-sized site until Google shows the new URLs, longer for larger sites) measure different things: indexing can switch within weeks while traffic recovery can take far longer, so plan and report on both.
  <br><sub>`D2-C915` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)</sub>
